editorNote: Issue #5 covers Monday, August 30 through Sunday, September 5, 1982. The desk leads with the August 30 Arcade Express report that Coleco's Donkey Kong cartridge for Atari VCS had compatibility trouble on some Model #2600 consoles. Around it, the issue treats Atari 5200 anticipation, Commodore 64 retail momentum, and September personal-computing software/peripheral ads as the week's practical computer-store texture.
morningLine: This week: Donkey Kong cartridge trouble lands in the trade press, fall-console talk starts crowding the counter, September computer magazines push databases and hard disks, An Officer and a Gentleman tops Labor Day weekend, and Jack & Diane takes the rock-radio No. 1 slot.

lead.headline: Donkey Kong Cartridge Trouble Hits the Counter
lead.summary: The August 30 Arcade Express opens with a retail headache: Coleco's Donkey Kong cartridge for the Atari VCS had proven unplayable on some Model #2600 consoles, turning one of the hottest arcade names into a compatibility story. For computer and game shops, the lesson is blunt: the home-arcade boom now depends on cartridges, hardware revisions, and return-counter trust as much as cabinet fame.
lead.confidence: Dated August 30, 1982 trade-newsletter source; compatibility wording follows the source summary
